$description: Meridian core tokens: type, space, radius, controls, layout, layers and motion. The same in every theme and accent; the compact density overrides the control group.

type.$description: Type: one family. Geist for every word and every number; Geist Mono for kickers, table heads in caps, identifiers and code.

font-sans.$description: Every word and every number. The app loads the face and names it --font-face-sans; the family name is the fallback.

font-mono.$description: Kickers (uppercase, tracked), identifiers, keys, hashes and code.

dev.zz.meridian.css: var(--font-face-mono, "Geist Mono"), ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

text-2xs.$description: Axis ticks, eyebrows and legends: the smallest text, never body copy.

text-xs.$description: Captions, meta lines, badges and dense table cells.

text-sm.$description: Table cells, secondary copy and small controls.

text-base.$description: Body copy and controls: the inherited size.

text-lg.$description: Card titles that lead a section, dialog titles.

text-2xl.$description: The metric figure: the number a tile exists to show.

text-page.$description: The page title: one per screen.

text-hero.$description: The hero figure: the one number a page leads with, in its featured card.

text-display.$description: Screens outside the shell (sign-in, not found) and the Atlas front door: one sentence at poster size.

weight-medium.$description: Labels, controls, navigation and emphasis inside a sentence.

weight-semibold.$description: Titles and figures. The heaviest weight in the system.

tracking-display.$description: Display titles and figures: large type set loose reads as a price tag.

tracking-caps.$description: Mono kickers and table heads in caps.

space.$description: Space: a 4px scale. The step is the multiple of 4 (space-6 is 24px); half steps exist below 8px only.

space-0-5.$description: Hairline gaps: a dot beside its label.

space-1.$description: Icon to text inside a badge.

space-1-5.$description: Icon to label inside a control.

space-3.$description: Inside dense controls and list rows.

space-4.$description: Card padding in compact density; the gap between cards on phones.

space-5.$description: Between a card title and its content.

space-6.$description: Card padding; the gap between cards.

space-8.$description: The page gutter on wide screens.

space-12.$description: Above a page title on standalone screens.

space-16.$description: Section rhythm in the Atlas and standalone screens.

space-24.$description: The largest step: the Atlas front door.

radius.$description: Radius: five steps and the pill. Nested corners step down one so the inner edge stays concentric.

radius-xs.$description: Marks inside a control: a checkbox, a bar end, a kbd.

radius-xl.$description: Dialogs, sheets, the featured card and the sign-in panel.

radius-full.$description: Pills, avatars, switches, status dots: roundness that means something.

blur.$description: Blur: the frost behind glass. Only translucent layers over moving content use it: the rail, the stuck top bar, the shell tools. A scrim only dims: blurring the whole page behind a dialog or the phone rail cost a phone more than 100 ms on every open.

blur-md.$description: Small glass: the shell tools, a floating control.

blur-xl.$description: Large glass: the rail and the stuck top bar, where whole cards pass beneath.

control.$description: Controls: three heights and the density-dependent rhythm of tables and cards. Compact density redefines this group.

control-lg.$description: Primary actions on standalone screens; the touch target.

stack-gap.$description: Between rows of cards and between cards in a row.

layout.$description: Layout: the shell and the two content widths.

assistant-width.$description: The assistant panel as a third column of the shell, from 1024px; below that it is a sheet no wider than the viewport.

rail-collapsed.$description: The navigation rail, collapsed to icons.

data-width.$description: Dashboards fill the canvas at every size: no cap, so a 2560px screen shows more, not a centred strip. The value is the width the layout is designed at; the CSS is 100%.

stage-width.$description: A standalone screen (sign in, not found): one sentence and one panel read as a pair, so they stay within this width and centre.

reading-width.$description: Forms, documents and settings: about ninety characters of body text.

gutter.$description: Space between the content and the window or rail.

layer-rail.$description: The navigation rail and its drawer on small screens.

layer-sticky.$description: The masthead once the page scrolls.

layer-popover.$description: Menus, selects and popovers, above an open dialog.

motion.$description: Motion: three jobs (arrive, answer, float), durations for each job and three curves. Reduced motion collapses every duration and delay to zero.

dur-press.$description: A control giving under the pointer.

dur-hover.$description: Colour and outline changes on hover and selection.

dur-enter.$description: Overlays and rows arriving; indicators sliding.

dur-exit.$description: Overlays leaving: menus, popovers, dialogs and the scrim go faster than they came.

dur-exit-sheet.$description: A sheet leaving over its own distance.

dur-grow.$description: Data arriving: a bar growing, a line drawing, a figure counting.

stagger.$description: Between siblings that arrive in reading order.

stagger-bar.$description: Columns of a chart growing one after another; many, so the step is small.

ease-out.$description: Everything that arrives: fast, then settles. The default curve.

ease-in-out.$description: Things that move from one place to another while visible.

ease-spring.$description: Only what should feel physical: the navigation marker, a switch thumb.

dur-loop-shimmer.$description: One pass of a skeleton's shimmer.

dur-loop-pulse.$description: One breath of a live dot: slow enough to sit in the corner of the eye.
